subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Outrage as Engagement
description: Learn Outrage as Engagement in one minute.

hook.text: Angry posts get more shares than happy ones. Platforms learned to amplify outrage because it drives clicks.

buildup.text: Research shows content that triggers moral outrage gets 20% more engagement per emotional word.

discovery.text: Facebook's own internal research confirmed that its algorithm promoted divisive content because it performed better.

twist.text: Facebook knew this was happening, tested fixes, and shelved them because they reduced engagement metrics.

climax.text: When outrage drives revenue, the platform has a financial incentive to keep you angry.

punchline.text: Outrage sells. The algorithm delivers it.

quiz.question: Why do social media algorithms tend to amplify outrage?
options: Outrage generates more engagement and keeps users on the platform longer
Platforms are required by law to show controversial content
